references.text: Moses gave the command that the blessing should be placed on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal—the Samaritans regarded Gerizim as their holy place of worship ([ref:Deut 11:29|Deuteronomy 11:29]).

God chose one specific place where His name would dwell, and there the Israelites were to bring their offerings—this became the basis for the Jews' insistence on Jerusalem as the proper place of worship ([ref:Deut 12:5-11|Deuteronomy 12:5-11]).
The tribes were ordered to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people, which gave this mountain special sacred significance for the Samaritans ([ref:Deut 27:12|Deuteronomy 27:12]).
Joshua fulfilled Moses' command at Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, confirming the religious importance of these mountains ([ref:Josh 8:33|Joshua 8:33]).
Jotham called out to the people from the top of Mount Gerizim, confirming the mountain's prominent place in Israel's history and Samaritan tradition ([ref:Judg 9:7|Judges 9:7]).
Solomon prayed that God's eyes would be turned toward the temple in Jerusalem, and that prayers directed to this place would be heard ([ref:1 Kings 8:29-30|1 Kings 8:29-30]).
God promised that His name would dwell in the temple in Jerusalem forever—this was the basis for the Jewish claim that Jerusalem was the right place of worship ([ref:1 Kings 9:3|1 Kings 9:3]).
Jerusalem was chosen by God as the place for His temple, unlike all other places ([ref:2 Chron 6:6|2 Chronicles 6:6]).
The Samaritans wished to participate in building the temple in Jerusalem but were rejected by the Jews—this deepened the religious division between the two groups ([ref:Ezra 4:1-3|Ezra 4:1-3]).
The psalmist expresses joy at going to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, where the tribes go up to praise the name of the Lord ([ref:Psa 122:1-4|Psalms 122:1-4]).

Jesus answered the Samaritan woman that a time is coming when neither this mountain nor Jerusalem will be the decisive place of worship, but true worshipers will worship in spirit and truth ([ref:John 4:21-24|John 4:21-24]).
